note: The DAILY UPDATE'S WATCHLIST SCREENSHOT: a dated, per-ticker market read of the author's own names. The daily and mid-week updates carry a TradingView screenshot of his watchlist, one chart per ticker, each with the ticker's change and the change percentage. Every row was read off the frame by eye at high magnification -- and two of the first readings were then CORRECTED against the pixels (see `corrections`).

frames.panes: 4 across, 4 rows centred: the last row holds three, at 135, 405 and 675
4 across, 2 rows; the last row holds two, centred at 270 and 540
4 across, 2 full rows and a third row holding one pane, centred at 405

corrections.how: The first reading was taken off the whole frame, where the last glyph is a blur. At 8x the pixels read X N D U -- the fourth glyph has a ROUNDED bottom, which is a U and not a D. The OCR read it 'XNDU' at every crop width from 36 to 62 px and every scale from 3x to 6x, and 'XNDU' is a listed ticker, so the reading stands and the hand reading was wrong.

The first reading was taken off the whole frame, where the red ink's leading digit is a smudge. At 8x the pixels read '-0.91 (8.46%)' -- the first digit of the percentage has a waist, which is an 8 and not a 0. The OCR read 8.46 at every crop width from 40 to 60 px and every scale from 3x to 6x.

At 24x the pixels read S Q M -- the Q's TAIL falls below the other two glyphs and a crop that ended above it showed an 'O'. The Q is the one glyph of the three that reaches lowest, so a crop has to run to the baseline and not stop at the letters' height. SQM is a listed ticker and SOM is not, which is what the market's own list said too.

The first reading was taken off the whole frame, where the '1' of '10.19' is a hairline. At 8x the pixels read '+10.19 (8.66%)' -- the second glyph is a 1 and not a 9, because it has no left shoulder and it sits at the same height as the 0 beside it.

notes: The screens are DARK (white text on a black chart) and the OCR needs the region inverted to read them well.

The ticker labels are THIRTY pixels tall, against the eight to thirteen of the panel video frames -- which is why this screenshot is the better source for a dated market read than the panel reader is.

Each chart carries the ticker, the date, the change, the change percentage and the price. A row that does not fill the screen's width is CENTRED -- one pane at 405, two at 270 and 540, three at 135, 405 and 675 -- which is why the pane origins are a HALF-pane grid and not the four-column grid.
The reader does NOT read the price: it is in a box on the chart rather than in the header, and it is a reading of the chart rather than of the header.
